fields.value: W. B. Yeats was an Irish poet, playwright, and critic. He was born in Sandymount, Dublin, on 13 June 1865. He died at Roquebrune in France on 28 January 1939. He led the Irish Literary Revival (a movement to renew Irish writing) and won the Nobel Prize in 1923.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Sri Aurobindo was an Indian philosopher, poet, and nationalist. He was born in Calcutta on 15 August 1872 and died in Pondicherry on 5 December 1950. He studied at Cambridge, then joined the freedom movement in Bengal. After 1910 he lived in Pondicherry and taught Integral Yoga (a path meant to change life on earth).

fields.value: UGC NET asks him under Unit II (Poetry) for Savitri, and under Unit I (Drama) for the plays. Essays on the Gita and The Life Divine belong with Unit IV (prose that is not fiction). fields.value: Ezra Pound was an American poet and a shaper of modernism (a new style that breaks old forms). He was born in Hailey, Idaho, in 1885 and died in Venice in 1972. fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Lorraine Hansberry was an American playwright and a civil rights activist. She was born in Chicago in 1930 and died in New York in 1965. She was the first Black woman to have a play produced on Broadway. Her family had already fought a whites only housing rule in the Supreme Court case Hansberry versus Lee.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks her under Unit 1 (Drama). One set question asks which poem is the epigraph of A Raisin in the Sun. The answer is Langston Hughes's Harlem, also called A Dream Deferred.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps
fields.value: She lived from 1930 to 1965. A Raisin in the Sun opened in 1959. Les Blancs reached Broadway in 1970, after her death. | Les Blancs was completed and staged/published after her death, with editorial collaboration.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Edward Wadie Said was a Palestinian American critic and teacher. He was born in Jerusalem in 1935 and died in New York in 2003. He taught English and comparative literature at Columbia University. Orientalism made him a founder of postcolonial studies, the reading of books through empire and power.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Said in Unit 8 (Literary Criticism), inside postcolonial theory. Questions test Orientalism in 1978, Foucault, and Gramsci. They also test Culture and Imperialism in 1993.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: bell hooks was the pen name of Gloria Jean Watkins, an American feminist writer and teacher. She was born in Hopkinsville, Kentucky, in 1952 and died in Berea in 2021. She printed the pen name in small letters so the ideas would matter more than the person. She chose the name to honor her great-grandmother.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET should place her in Unit IX (Literary Theory) and Unit VII (Cultural Studies). A database label calls two of these books poetry. They are prose books. A 2012 question on the word womanist points to Alice Walker, not to hooks.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Carol Ann Duffy is a Scottish poet and playwright. She was born in Glasgow in 1955 and is still living. She was Poet Laureate (the official national poet) from 2009 to 2019. She was the first woman, and the first poet born in Scotland, to hold that post.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET places her in Unit II (Poetry). Questions ask students to order her books by year. They also ask how The World's Wife retells myth. She is a living poet of our time, not a poet of 1914-1945.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps
fields.value: Laureate Duffy: Nude in 1985, Wife in 1999, Rapture in 2005, Bees in 2011. | The World’s Wife reworks myths and historical narratives from women’s perspectives. | Uses dramatic voices and mythic/historical revision; overlaps postmodern and contemporary poetry.
